summary: Two batch items. First, the four follow-up gaps registered by the knowledge-1 correction are answered with explicit resolved judgments: for each recorded use the premise correction changes only explanatory wording, not evidence or conclusions — the receipts never contained a leader change inside a pending window, so the corrected mechanism (caller sends on n.propc; the run loop simply is not receiving while its gate variable is disarmed) is consistent with every index each interpretation cites. Second, a successor experiment is submitted that closes the two remaining limitations from the previous revision: the same invocation on the re-added voter is issued with a context that never expires (observed 2000 ms, payload absent), and after the forced leader change the harness records whether that still-pending invocation was admitted by the re-armed gate (field pending) and whether its payload then committed; the earlier misleading tail that stopped the node and emitted an 'unbounded_release' label for an already-returned call is removed. Fifteen comparisons are evaluated, each on a uniquely named event so no comparison sees another operation's result; a local dry run of the fixed harness produced returned=false at 2001 ms with leader 1 stable, pending=false with err empty at 3624 ms after the leader change, and the payload committed on all three nodes.
